verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              स्वराष्ट्रात्परराष्ट्राच्च कोशं संजनयेन्नृपः । कोशाद्धि धर्मः कौन्तेय राज्यमूलं च वर्धते ॥१॥
verses.english: Janaka said You have, O foremost of Rishis, said that Unity is the attribute of that which is Indestructible and variety or multiplicity is the attribute of what is known as Destructible. I have not, however, clearly understood the nature of these two. Doubts are still in my mind.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्संजनयेत्कोशं सत्कृत्य परिपालयेत् । परिपाल्यानुतनुयादेष धर्मः सनातनः ॥२॥
verses.english: Ignorant men consider the Soul as endued with multiplicity. They, however, who are endued with knowledge and wisdom consider the Soul to be one and the same. I, however, have a very dull understanding. I am, therefore, unable to understand how all this can take place.

verses.sanskrit: न कोशः शुद्धशौचेन न नृशंसेन जातुचित् । मध्यमं पदमास्थाय कोशसंग्रहणं चरेत् ॥३॥
verses.english: I have almost forgotten the causes also that you have attributed to the unity and the multiplicity of the Indestructible and the Destructible on account of the restlessness of my understanding.

verses.sanskrit: अबलस्य कुतः कोशो ह्यकोशस्य कुतो बलम् । अबलस्य कुतो राज्यमराज्ञः श्रीर्भवेत्कुतः ॥४॥
verses.english: I, therefore, wish to hear you once more discourse to me on those subjects of unity and multiplicity, on him who is gifted with knowledge, on what is shorn of knowledge, on Individual Soul, Knowledge, Ignorance, on Indestructible, Destructible, and the Sankhya and the Yoga systems, in detail and separately and agreeable to the truth.

verses.sanskrit: उच्चैर्वृत्तेः श्रियो हानिर्यथैव मरणं तथा । तस्मात्कोशं बलं मित्रमथ राजा विवर्धयेत् ॥५॥
verses.english: Vashishtha said I shall tell you what you ask. Listen, however, to me, O king, as I explain to you the practices of Yoga separately.

verses.sanskrit: हीनकोशं हि राजानमवजानन्ति मानवाः । न चास्याल्पेन तुष्यन्ति कार्यमप्युत्सहन्ति च ॥६॥
verses.english: Contemplation, which forms an obligatory practice with Yogins, is their highest power, Those conversant with Yoga say that that Contemplation is of two sorts.

verses.sanskrit: श्रियो हि कारणाद्राजा सक्रियां लभते पराम् । सास्य गृहति पापानि वासो गुह्यमिव स्त्रियाः ॥७॥
verses.english: One is the concentration of the mind, and the other is called Pranayama (suppression of vital airs). Pranayama is said to be real; while concentration of mind is unsubstantial to it.

verses.sanskrit: ऋद्धिमस्यानु तप्यन्ते पुरा विप्रकृता नराः । शालावृका इवाजस्त्रं जिघांसुमेव विन्दति ॥८॥
verses.english: Excepting the three times when a man passes urine and stools and eats, one should devote his entire time to contemplation.

verses.sanskrit: ईदृशस्य कुतो राज्ञः सुखं भवति भारत । उद्यच्छेदेव न नमेदुद्यमो ह्येव पौरुषम् ॥९॥
verses.english: Withdrawing the senses from their objects by the help of the mind, one gifted with intelligence, having made oneself pure, should, according to the twenty-two modes of transmitting the Prana breath, unite the Individual Soul with That which is above the four and twentieth topic which is regarded by the wise as living in every part of the body and as above decay and destruction.

verses.sanskrit: अप्यपर्वणि भज्येत न नमेतेह कस्यचित् । अप्यरण्यं समाश्रित्य चरेन्मृगगणैः सह ॥१०॥
verses.english: It is by means of those twenty-two modes that the Soul may always be known. It is certain that this practice of Yoga is his whose mind is never possessed by evil passions. It is not any other person's.

verses.sanskrit: न त्वेवोज्झितमर्यादैर्दस्युभिः सहितश्चरेत् । दस्यूनां सुलभा सेना रौद्रकर्मसु भारत ॥११॥
verses.english: Freed from all attachments, abstemious in diet, and controlling all the senses, one should fix his mind on the Soul, during the first and the last part of the night, after having, O king of Mithila, stopped the functions of all the senses, quieted the mind by the understanding, and assumed a posture as motionless as that of stone.

verses.sanskrit: एकान्ततो ह्यमर्यादात्सर्वोऽप्युद्विजते जनः । दस्यवोऽप्यभिशङ्कन्ते निरनुक्रोशकारिणः ॥१२॥
verses.english: When men of knowledge, conversant with the rules of Yoga, become as fixed as a stake of wood, and as immovable as a mountain, then they are said to be in Yoga.

verses.sanskrit: स्थापयेदेव मर्यादां जनचित्तप्रसादिनीम् । अल्पेऽप्यर्थे च मर्यादा लोके भवति पूजिता ॥१३॥
verses.english: When one does not hear, and smell and taste, and see; when one does not feel any touch; when one's mind is perfectly free from every purpose; when one is not conscious of any thing, when one cherishes no thought, when one becomes like a piece of wood, then is he called by the wise to be in perfect Yoga.

verses.sanskrit: नायं लोकोऽस्ति न पर इति व्यवसितो जनः । नालं गन्तुं हि विश्वासं नास्तिके भयशङ्किते ॥१४॥
verses.english: At such a time one shines like a limp that burns in a place where blows no wind; at such a time one becomes freed even from his subtile form, and perfectly at one with Brahma. When one acquires such progress, he has no longer to ascend or to fall among intermediate beings.

verses.sanskrit: यथा सद्भिः परादानमहिंसा दस्युभिः कृता । अनुरज्यन्ति भूतानि समर्यादेषु दस्युषु ॥१५॥
verses.english: When persons like ourselves say that there has been a complete identification of Knower, the Known, and Knowledge, then is the Yogin said to see the Supreme Self.

verses.sanskrit: अयुद्ध्यमानस्य वधो दारामर्षः कृतघ्नता । ब्रह्मवित्तस्य चादानं निःशेषकरणं तथा ॥१६॥
verses.english: While in Yoga, the Supreme Soul shows itself in the Yogin's heart like a burning fire, or like the bright Sun or like the lightning's spark in the firmament.

verses.sanskrit: स्त्रिया मोषः पतिस्थानं दस्युष्वेतद्विगर्हितम् । संश्लेषं च परस्त्रीभिर्दस्युरेतानि वर्जयेत् ॥१७॥
अभिसंदधते ये च विश्वासायास्य मानवाः । अशेषमेवोपलभ्य कुर्वन्तीति विनिश्चयः ॥१८॥
verses.english: That Supreme Soul which is Unborn and which is the essence of nectar, which is seen by great Brahmanas gifted with intelligence and wisdom and conversant with the Vedas, is subtiler than what is subtile and greater than what is great. That Soul, though living in all creatures, is not seen by them.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्सशेषं कर्तव्यं स्वाधीनमपि दस्युभिः । न बलस्थोऽहमस्मीति नृशंसानि समाचरेत् ॥१९॥
verses.english: The Creator of the worlds, He is seen only by a person gifted with wealth of intelligence when helped by the lamp of the mind. He lives on the other shore of the Darkness and is above the Ishvara.

verses.sanskrit: स शेषकारिणस्तत्र शेषं पश्यन्ति सर्वशः । निःशेषकारिणो नित्यं निःशेषकरणाद्भयम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: Persons conversant with the Vedas and endued with omniscience call Him the remover of Darkness, stainless, above Darkness, and with and without attributes.
